findings.text: the head arm's file list was derived by a text grep (reckon.crew.recovery|crew import recovery|from reckon.crew.recovery) that matches only single-name imports, so it ran 93 files while an AST scan of the same tree finds 94 tests/ files importing reckon.crew.recovery: seven importers were never measured — including tests/test_review_role_is_not_reviewed.py, which drives the modified recovery.dispatch_awaiting_reviews at line 228 — and six grepped files do not import the module at all; my head probe of the seven excluded files passes (94 passed, EXIT=0), so the delta survives the gap, but the recorded population is not the one the done-when names.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against e2c4a662; it carries the repair pass, the composer's negative_control declaration (repair.py:297), the _review_tree working-directory guard (recovery.py:215) and four driving tests, with the commit body naming each change rather than leaving it to be inferred.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done-when's driving test passes as recorded (tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py:238; reproduced 4 passed, EXIT=0), and the added-failure claim re-derives to zero through the store's own reader (review.py:870) from the reviewed run's baseline_suite/after_suite logs, whose 35 base and 31 head failure ids the manifest transcribes exactly.
item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal is one repair node per finding-bearing review round, and the landed change wires exactly that: recovery.py:1747-1770 runs dispatch_repair_for_run (recovery.py:1429) for every live pointer and reports each composed repair beside the review pass.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read in full; it records the focused gate and both arm logs with their EXIT= lines and names the negative-control mutation it declares, and its one evidence shortfall is the finding below.
item_verdicts.write_paths: Read the manifest's declared scope and the diff: git diff --name-status e2c4a662..1fb5dd19 lists exactly recovery.py, repair.py and tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, and the reviewed worktree is clean at 1fb5dd19.

justifications.durability: The four tests re-derive the finding id rule independently (tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py:178) and the declared mutation reddens the three-finding test's dispatch-count assertion (arm-red.log), while the redispatch-after-death branch (recovery.py:1420-1425) and the _review_tree guard (recovery.py:215) carry no test.
justifications.evidence: The focused gate and the zero-added-failure delta both reproduce (4 passed, EXIT=0; 0 added ids through review.py:870), but the arm population came from a text grep that missed seven importing test files, so the recorded head arm measured 93 of the 94 tests/ files that import the changed module.
justifications.fit: The pass reuses the module's pointer-mutation and sweep-report idioms, and its new names (dispatch_repair_for_run, _repair_in_flight, REPAIR_DISPATCH_FIELD) name mechanisms with no plan, ticket or version identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: recovery.py:1747-1770 composes at most one repair per live pointer through compose_repair_for_run and reports it beside the review pass, which is the goal's sentence.
justifications.scope_discipline: The diff touches exactly the three declared paths, and both supporting changes are implied by the goal — repair.py:297 declares the negative control the composed scope requires, and recovery.py:215 stops a repair's head being read from the sweeping process's own working directory.
